During my first term, I took monumental action to strengthen America's foster care and adoption systems by signing into law the landmark Family First Prevention Services Act -- the most sweeping reform of Federal child welfare policy in decades. This law utilizes proven intervention methods to keep families intact and prevent unnecessary separation. This term, I remain firmly committed to continuing this vital work alongside First Lady Melania Trump. Just last week, I signed an Executive Order on Fostering the Future for American Children and Families, to harness Federal support, technology, and strategic partnerships to provide young Americans in, or transitioning out of, the foster-care system with the tools they need to become successful adults. name: EPA Rollbacks
title:
The federal Environmental Protection Agency has rolled back rules restricting climate warming emissions at electrical power plants, including those in Georgia.  

The rules the EPA ended this week date from the Biden administration and would have required coal and natural gas-fired power plants to restrict carbon emissions starting in 2030. 

That was about the same time Georgia Power had planned to shutter its two largest coal plants — Plant Bowen, which is north of Atlanta, and Plant Scherer, just north of Macon. But now with the data center boom, Georgia Power is keeping the plants running.

With the help of a third coal plant over the border in Alabama, Georgia Power hopes to meet fully 70% of the data center demand.

title: Today’s actions by US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) represent a… | Michelle Bloodworth
description:
Today’s actions by US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) represent a big win for electricity consumers, grid reliability, and America’s energy dominance.
  
I want to commend President Trump and EPA for repealing the Biden Carbon Rule and proposing to rescind the Endangerment Finding for greenhouse gas emissions from power plants.

The Carbon Rule would have left electricity providers with just two options: shutter their coal power plants by 2032 or attempt to comply by installing carbon capture and storage technology that is exorbitantly expensive and not adequately demonstrated. Retrofitting a single coal power plant with carbon capture technology could cost several billion dollars, in some cases exceeding the original cost of the power plant.

At a moment when data centers, artificial intelligence, and advanced manufacturing are driving unprecedented electricity demand, we cannot afford to force the retirement of reliable, dispatchable coal generation.

By overturning this regulatory overreach, the Trump Administration is demonstrating its commitment to ensuring America can benefit from our abundant coal reserves and the reliable power coal provides.

America's energy future depends on getting rid of bad regulations and policies.
